pullRequests.body:
## Summary

Pilot duration-weighted sharding in a separate Actions workflow. Four Ubuntu jobs run the complete Node coverage suite between them. The workflow runs an unsharded control on the same commit and checks that all 46 files completed exactly once with matching test counts per file.

```text
measured file durations → longest files assigned first
                        → four shards with the lightest shard taking the next file
                        → compare file reports against the unsharded control
```

Each job publishes its measured file durations for the next profiling iteration. The initial weights come from a complete local coverage run. A newly added file gets a size-based estimate until measured.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Pilot duration-weighted sharding for the Node coverage suite."
impact: "Collects CI timing and test-count evidence for the same suite in both execution layouts."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- Latest 150 Actions runs include 18 completed full-suite Quality PR runs, with 226 seconds at p50 and 297 seconds at p95.
- Local unsharded profiling completed 46 files and 918 tests in 175.33 seconds. The largest file, release publication, measured 110.25 seconds under the unsharded workload.
- In the same timing profile, the largest cumulative file load fell from 215.49 seconds for alphabetical round-robin assignment to 121.72 seconds for weighted assignment. These are modeled loads and the hosted workflow measures elapsed time.
- The parity check accepted the measured partition and failed when a file report was removed. Workflow syntax, types, and lint passed locally.
- Hosted test execution fell from 217 seconds unsharded to 81 seconds on the slowest shard. The four shard steps took 81, 41, 47, and 38 seconds. Including queue, setup and upload, the comparable results were ready after 238 seconds versus 104 seconds. Combined runner usage for the four test jobs was 289 seconds versus 235 seconds. The pilot also runs the control and evidence check. [Hosted pilot](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44928001470)
- The hosted parity check passed for all 46 files and 918 tests. The longest shard spent approximately 80 seconds inside the release publication integration file, above the 30-second test budget.
- Required Quality and metadata checks passed. The separate container security scan reported the same 19 vulnerability, severity, package, and version combinations as the PR base. [Quality](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44928001356) · [PR scan](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44928001357) · [Base scan](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44926243148)

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way

**Blast radius** Pilot workflows only. The existing full Quality workflow and required status checks still gate merges. The pilot runs for changes to its own files and can be dispatched manually. Per-shard coverage reports are individual, with the aggregate coverage report supplied by the existing full suite.

## Summary

Split the publication integration suite into four independently schedulable test files for inspection, registry validation, writes and recovery, and write guards. They share the existing fixture, with a fresh Git repository and mock transport for each case. The coverage command still discovers all four files.

This PR stacks on #148. It replaces the original suite's timing weight with measurements for the four files so the existing pilot distributes them across runners.


The follow-up commit reads each proposal commit once for its tree, message, and parent IDs. Approval verification continues to perform the same Git identity, history, remote evidence, and freshness checks.


Quality now runs the four coverage shards in parallel with formatting, lint, types, architecture, docs, and commit-policy checks. The required `verify` status confirms those checks and the complete shard inventory. The two unsharded CI runs are removed. Local `pnpm verify` still produces a combined coverage report.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: "Run the full behavioral suite as four required Quality shards."
impact: "Removes duplicate CI test runs, keeps all behavioral cases required, and reduces duplicate local Git reads during approval."
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- The original hosted pilot's slowest shard took 81 seconds to execute tests, about 80 seconds of which was the publication suite. Queueing took 3 seconds, runner setup 17 seconds, and artifact upload and runner cleanup 3 seconds combined. [Parent pilot](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44928001470)
- The four local files ran all 57 original cases. Their names and multiplicities matched, and their test definitions and assertions were moved verbatim.
- In the original suite, fixture setup accounted for 46.6 of 190.8 summed case-seconds and directory removal for 1.7 seconds. The setup included 17.6 seconds preparing proposals and 25.2 seconds verifying approvals and rendering notes. Concurrent spans overlap in wall time.
- In the 14 write-and-recovery cases, the 124 in-test approval verification calls took 104.2 of 137.7 summed case-seconds. The split preserves those checks.
- One local coverage on/off pair took 97.7 seconds and 93.5 seconds with the same 57 cases. The hosted comparison keeps coverage enabled.
- On GitHub Actions, the slowest test step fell from 81 to 68 seconds and all shard results were ready in 88 seconds, down from 104. The four jobs consumed 277 runner-seconds, down from 289. On the new critical path, queueing took 2 seconds, runner setup 15 seconds, and upload and cleanup 3 seconds. The longest publication file took 54 seconds, down from 80 seconds for the original combined suite. [Hosted comparison](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44937531479)
- The hosted parity check and an independent replay both verified all 49 files and 918 tests. The existing local and hosted Quality checks passed. The separate container-security scan failed with the same 19 findings as the parent pilot. [Quality](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44937531432) · [Container security](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44937531431)
- In a local sequential comparison on four pinned CPUs, three file workers finished the busiest shard in 44.25 seconds and two in 56.75 seconds. Both passed all 339 cases. The pilot keeps the current worker setting.

- The local approval profile recorded 9 fewer Git subprocesses per verification in both prototype runs. Wall-clock times overlapped across baseline and prototype runs. All 14 write-and-recovery cases passed in both prototype runs, and 12 targeted approval guard tests passed.

- The follow-up commit passed local verification with 918 behavioral tests and 22 architecture cases. [Hosted run for the follow-up commit](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44940601276)

- Quality passed in 1m30s with four sharded test jobs, no unsharded behavioral run, and the existing required `verify` check. The published reports account for 918 tests across 49 files. [Sharded Quality](https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/actions/runs/44941444966)

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way

**Blast radius** Quality workflow, test scheduling, and the local proposal-tree reader. The required check name and existing release-PR exception are preserved.

## Summary

Use the `RELEASE_CONTAINER_SCAN` GitHub Actions repository variable to control the standalone container vulnerability workflow and the release publication scan.

```text
RELEASE_CONTAINER_SCAN=true or unset → run the existing vulnerability scans
RELEASE_CONTAINER_SCAN=false → skip vulnerability scans
Release publication → always run container smoke tests and verify image identity
```

The repository variable is currently `false`. Set it to `true` or remove it in **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables** to restore scanning. An explicit `false` applies across all releases. Publication records when it skips the scan.

## Evidence

- **Before** The standalone scan reported ten High findings and exited with code 1.
- **After** Workflow fixtures verified that an explicit `false` pauses both scan paths and that `true`, an unset variable, and unrecognized values enable them. All 25 focused publication tests passed.
- The actual `v0.6.0` image passed the smoke suite from its source checkout. Its archive config digest matched the previous scan.

## Merge Danger

**Door** Set the repository variable to `true` or remove it to restore scanning on the next run. Images published while it is `false` can ship without vulnerability scan evidence.

**Blast radius** Container vulnerability scans on PRs, `main`, scheduled and manually dispatched runs, plus container release publication.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Control container vulnerability scanning with a repository Actions variable.
impact: Set RELEASE_CONTAINER_SCAN to false to pause container vulnerability scanning across CI and release publication. Container smoke tests and image digest verification continue during publication.
required_action: null
```

Trusted main    → pinned producer → candidate build and verified publication

**Blast radius** Manual rehearsals and the trusted self-publication job.

Refs #150.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Prepare provider identity checks for the planned repository slug change.
impact: The provider accepts both slugs only with the stable repository ID while current consumer pins and GHCR naming remain unchanged.
required_action: Coordinate the remaining self-release and consumer workflow updates before renaming the provider repository.
```

## Summary

```text
release-log / ID 1449550207
  accepts current name:  lhajoosten/release-log
  accepts next name:     lhajoosten/rolling-release
  preserves current consumer workflow pins and GHCR image path
```

The trusted self-release config and workflow guards accept either provider slug only when the numeric repository ID remains `1449550207`. The self-release caller also gates by that stable ID.

## Evidence

- **Before:** self-release identity checks accepted only `lhajoosten/release-log`.
- **After:** focused tests accept both names and reject an unknown name or mismatched repository ID.
- **Checks:** `node --test tests/provider-identity.test.ts`, TypeScript `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint on the changed TypeScript files, formatting check, and `git diff --check` passed. Full `pnpm check` could not run in the isolated clone because its dependency store is unavailable.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change does not rename the repository, change consumer `uses:` references, or move the GHCR image. Existing consumers keep their current workflow and image paths. This prep PR alone does not make provider self-release or new consumer setup work after the rename.

**Blast Radius:** provider

**Required follow-up before cutover:**

- Update both the caller's embedded `CONFIGURATION` and `release-log.config.json` to the new repository name before self-release runs. `scripts/self-release.ts` still requires `GITHUB_REPOSITORY === configuration.repository`; `GitHubProposalRepository.verifyRepository()` also requires API `full_name` to equal the configured name.
- Preserve and verify historical proposal replay across the name change. `src/snapshot/replay.ts` compares the captured configuration digest with the expected configuration, so simply changing the repository name makes old snapshots incompatible. Do not rewrite captured snapshots; design and test a compatibility path that uses their recorded producer runtimes.
- Update provider-path handling for consumer callers: `src/metadata-onboarding.ts` accepts only the old workflow path, `src/release-preflight.ts` emits only the old path, and `src/proposal/tool-pins.ts` validates that old path. Test old pinned producer SHAs and new slug pins through onboarding, preflight and replay.
- Confirm old-URL clone and checkout operations still fetch historical immutable producer SHAs after rename, or update them as part of the coordinated migration. Current references include `scripts/install-producer-runtimes.ts` and the reusable workflow checkout.

**Cutover sequence and hold:**

1. Stage consumer PRs with their new immutable workflow pins while the old slug still works.
2. Complete and merge the provider and historical-replay follow-ups before renaming.
3. Rename the provider repository to `rolling-release`.
4. Merge the staged consumer PRs promptly. Their new `uses: lhajoosten/rolling-release/.github/workflows/...` paths cannot resolve until after the rename, and existing old-slug pins will not follow the rename.

Keep GHCR at `ghcr.io/lhajoosten/release-log` through this cutover.

Supersedes #142 on current main with a commit that follows the repository's commit conventions. The policy and pinned Action revision are carried forward.

## Summary

```text
Quality → SHA-pinned lint-action → source findings in report-only mode
  ├─ cyclomatic complexity
  ├─ cognitive complexity
  └─ source duplication
```

The pilot scans supported source under `src/`. TypeScript retains its cyclomatic limit of 10. Other cyclomatic limits and all cognitive limits use 12. Duplication starts at 50 shared tokens.

This rollout introduces the policy. A manual Quality run on this branch exercises the scan. Ordinary pull requests start using the policy once it lands on their base branch.

The workflow pins the revision from https://github.com/lhajoosten/lint-gate/pull/11, stacked on https://github.com/lhajoosten/lint-gate/pull/8. The provider boundary remains an architecture check in https://github.com/lhajoosten/release-log/pull/144 and is recorded in https://github.com/lhajoosten/lint-gate/pull/9.

## Release context

```release-log
version: 1
audience: internal
summary: Pilot source complexity and duplication reporting in the Quality workflow.
impact: Maintainers get cognitive complexity, cyclomatic complexity, and duplication findings while evaluating report-only thresholds.
required_action: null
```

## Evidence

- `actionlint` passed for the branch and a clean merge preview against `main`.
- The pinned Action adapter scanned 91 TypeScript files in the merge preview. It reported 100 cyclomatic complexity findings, 71 cognitive complexity findings, and 16 duplication pairs with zero analysis errors.
- Rust and Python coverage passed through packaged CLI fixtures in the lint-action expansion. Release Log’s selected source is TypeScript.

## Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way. Reverting the workflow and policy removes the pilot.

**Blast radius** The Quality verification job.
